analysis: The method writeBytes takes a byte array buff, offset off, and length len. It uses instance variables arr (byte array) and pos (position index). Before calling System.arraycopy, it checks if (pos + len) > arr.length and calls resize to increase arr size, ensuring sufficient destination capacity. However, no checks are performed on the validity of buff, off, or len. The arraycopy API can throw NullPointerException if src or dest is null, ArrayStoreException for type mismatches, and IndexOutOfBoundsException for invalid indices or length. Since both arrays are byte[], ArrayStoreException is avoided. NullPointerException can occur if buff (parameter) is null or arr (instance) is null. IndexOutOfBoundsException can occur if off or len negative, off+len greater than buff.length, pos negative, or if dest capacity is insufficient (though resize attempts to prevent dest bounds issues, it may not cover all cases, e.g., negative pos).
answer:
NullPointerException: Condition not avoided (buff or arr can be null).
ArrayStoreException: Condition avoided (both arrays are byte[]).
IndexOutOfBoundsException: Condition not avoided (no checks on off, len, or pos negativity; off+len may exceed buff.length; pos negative not handled).
remark: NullPointerException is triggered if buff (the source array) is null or if arr (the destination array) is null. Since no null checks are performed, a null argument will cause the exception. IndexOutOfBoundsException is triggered if off or len are negative, if off+len exceeds buff.length, if pos is negative, or if dest capacity is not guaranteed despite the resize (e.g., if pos is negative, the condition (pos+len) > arr.length might be false and resize not called, leading to destPos negative).
